title: Tidy up
briefing: Your home directory is littered with log files. Time to file them away.
One wildcard can grab them all at once.
tips: `*` matches anything: `*.log` means every name ending in .log.
`mkdir NAME` makes a directory; `mv *.log NAME/` moves them all inside.
objective: Create a directory called logs and move every .log file in your home into it.
hints: First make somewhere to put them: a directory. Then move the files there.
`mkdir logs` makes the directory. `*.log` matches every log file at once.

reactions.say: readme.txt was not a .log — `*.log` shouldn't have touched it. Careful which wildcard you use.

explanation: The shell expands `*.log` to every matching name before mv even runs, so `mv *.log logs/` moves them in one shot. Wildcards (globs) are one of the biggest time-savers in the shell — and one of the easiest ways to move the wrong thing, so look before you glob.
